summary: Faraday Telecom: failover thundering-herd causing cross-tenant rate-limits and partial outage - post-incident follow-up
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 03:22 UTC Faraday Telecom experienced a partial service outage for inference requests. A scheduled maintenance window on a subset of Dedicated GPU pools triggered an automated drain of several nodes; the autoscaler inadvertently scaled down backup pools faster than expected, causing many customer requests to failover to hosted capacity in us-east. The hosted routing hit global soft rate-limits and a cascade of client retries produced a classic 'thundering herd' pattern.

Impact:
- 35% error rate (5xx/429) for Faraday's production traffic between 03:22–03:56 UTC.
- Increased tail latency for chat streaming; several streams truncated.
- Cross-tenant soft rate-limits engaged, affecting 12 other customers with transient 429s.
- Billing exposure observed due to repeated retries and duplicate completions for some requests.

Environment:
- prod us-east, Dedicated pools (dedicated-faraday-prod-pool) with fallback to hosted-api cluster-02.
- Model: redwood-rlhf-large-v2 pinned by customer.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Simulate drain of two dedicated GPU nodes serving a heavy prefix workload.
2) Force failover policy to routed-hosted when capacity under threshold.
3) Replay client behavior with aggressive retry (retry-after not respected).
4) Observe rate-limiter counters and queue saturation on hosted router.

Logs and traces referenced:
- Hosted router traces: trace-id 8b4f2a1b-03 (sample span links in confluence page).
- Autoscaler events: cluster-autoscaler logs 2026-03-10 03:20-03:40 UTC.
- Customer-provided SDK logs attached in support bundle (s3://support-bundles/faraday/128500/).
investigation_notes:
Timeline and primary hypothesis:
- 03:18 UTC: Scheduled maintenance job issued drain.
- 03:20 UTC: Autoscaler reconciler erroneously interpreted pool health as degraded and removed two warm spare nodes due to a config regression introduced in autoscaler PR 118.
- 03:22 UTC: Traffic overflowed to hosted-api cluster-02; global token bucket rate-limiter applied conservative per-customer limits.
- 03:24-03:40 UTC: Observed exponential retry patterns from Faraday SDK (client retry logic did not respect 'Retry-After' header due to older SDK version).
- 03:30 UTC: Queue depth spike on router and streaming connection resets.
Investigation confirmed via autoscaler leader logs and tracing. Key finding: autoscaler PR 118 modified drain behavior to prefer aggressive scale-down when average GPU utilization falls below 12% — in our scenario warm spares dropped below that threshold. Secondary contributing factor: SDK clients with aggressive retry policy and lack of exponential backoff.

Telemetry artifacts: grafana panels 'router-rate-limiter', 'autoscaler-reconcile', 'hosted-queue-depth' attached in incident runbook.
resolution_notes:
Mitigations applied during incident:
- 03:36 UTC: Support toggled fallback-policy to 'graceful' for Faraday, preventing further immediate failovers.
- 03:40 UTC: Temporary raise of per-customer rate-limit on hosted-api cluster-02 to accommodate inflight failovers while teams stabilized pools.
- 03:45 UTC: Autoscaler leader rolled back PR 118 and recomputed desired state; two warm spare nodes were restored.
- 03:50 UTC: Re-enabled normal routing; error rates and latencies returned to baseline by 03:56 UTC.
Post-incident actions implemented:
- Rollback of autoscaler PR 118 and a hotfix (PR 4331) to add safety gates to drain logic.
- Customer credits: applied a one-time invoice credit for duplicate-completion billing exposure (handled by Finance).
- Communication: sent customer-facing incident summary and remediation plan to Faraday CSM and engineering on 2026-03-11.
- SDK outreach: Customer engineering recommended to upgrade to SDK v2.3.1 which respects Retry-After and adds jitter to backoff.
postincident_actions: Add autoscaler drain safety gate: require min-warm-spares >= 2 before aggressive scale-down
Add runtime circuit-breaker to prevent single-customer failover floods from consuming hosted router token buckets
Rate-limiter instrumentation: expose per-customer retry amplification metric to Console
Customer outreach: scheduled technical review with Faraday engineers on 2026-03-18
Create runbook: 'handling-dedicated-to-hosted-failover' and link in routing runbooks
